marks.gloss_en: ומה המאמין בחולדה ובור כך -- המאמין בהקב"ה על אחת כמה וכמה: if one who trusted a weasel and a pit [as witnesses] is so [vindicated], one who trusts the Holy One all the more
R' Ami: see how great are people of faith -- from the weasel and the pit: if one who trusts a weasel and a pit [is so], one who trusts the Holy One, all the more so
כי הא דריש לקיש הוה מסדר מתניתיה ארבעין זימנין
רב אדא בר אהבה מסדר מתניתיה עשרין וארבע זימנין
Reish Lakish would review his mishna forty times, corresponding to the forty days the Torah was given, and go in before R' Yochanan
רבי חייא בר אבין אמר רב הונא, מהכא: וכיראתך עברתך
R' Yochanan: whoever justifies himself below, judgment is justified upon him from above (Ps 85:12)
ריש לקיש אמר מהכא: פגעת את שש ועשה צדק
Reish Lakish: from here -- 'You meet him who rejoices and does righteousness, those who remember You in Your ways' (Isa 64:4)
והיינו דאמר ריש לקיש משום בר קפרא: נאמרה עצירה בגשמים ונאמרה עצירה באשה
Reish Lakish: 'and He will close up the heavens' -- when the heavens are closed from bringing dew and rain, it is like a woman in labour who does not give birth
אִינִי? והא אוקים שמואל אמורא עליה ודרש: ויפתוהו בפיהם... ולבם לא נכון עמו... ואף על פי כן והוא רחום יכפר עון -- prayer without the heart is still forgiven
R' Ami: a person's prayer is heard only if he puts his soul in his palm (Lam 3:41)
לא קשיא: כאן ביחיד, כאן בציבור -- here of an individual, there of a community
Reish Lakish: a student whose study is hard on him as iron -- it is because his mishna is not set in order for him (Eccl 10:10)
his remedy: let him sit [and study] much (Eccl 10:10); all the more so had his mishna been in order from the start
Rava: a student whose study is hard on him as iron -- it is because his teacher does not show him a pleasant face (Eccl 10:10)
his remedy: let him bring many companions to [his teacher] (Eccl 10:10); all the more so had his deeds been proper before his teacher from the start
R' Ami: 'if the serpent bites without a whisper' (Eccl 10:11) -- a generation whose sky is like copper from bringing dew and rain is because there are no whisperers [of prayer] in the generation
their remedy: let them go to one who knows how to whisper (Job 36:33); and 'no advantage to the master of the tongue' -- one who could whisper and does not, what benefit has he?
and if he whispered and was not answered, his remedy: let him go to the pious one of the generation, who should increase prayer for him (Job 36:32; Jer 7:16)
and if he whispered and succeeded and grows haughty over it, he brings anger to the world -- 'the cattle also concerning the storm' (Job 36:33, read as 'provoking anger')
Rava: two scholars who live in one city and are not agreeable to one another in halakha provoke anger and bring it up (Job 36:33)

Reish Lakish (Eccl 10:11): in the future all the beasts will gather to the serpent and say: the lion tears and eats, the wolf mauls and eats, what benefit have you? it says: 'and there is no advantage to the master of the tongue'
R' Ami: rain falls only for the sake of people of faith (Ps 85:12)
